column1: # Game profile of Batman: Arkham Knight (Switch, update 1.0.5 = v327680; the base NSP is a 7 MB stub). Plays on the Mac
# Format: see dm/games/README.md; bring-up and measurements in README.md beside this file
# Rocksteady's Unreal Engine 3 (package version 864) with Wwise, CRI Sofdec movies and Scaleform menus, SDK 14.3.0.
# The shaders are the global shader cache (GlobalShaderCache-Switch.bin) and the combined one in the Oodle-compressed package CombinedShaderCache-Switch.xxx (shader_split.py ue3_shaders).
# The engine's allocator runs on the host (patches.py, hle_uemalloc.c layout UE3); the game's task ring gets barriers (patches.py)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# The NPDM declares 32 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main never sets a heap. With the engine's allocator on a host malloc zone (outside the guest block)
# the game maps almost nothing in the alias region, and on iOS the block, that heap and Metal share the app's address space: a 2 GB block with a 1.375 GB alias region,
# as pull request #384 found on an iPad, where Engage's 5 GB block ran the heap out of address space (README.md, Memory). The node area is cut for this sdk build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py)

column2: Batman: Arkham Knight shaders (Unreal Engine 3 global and combined shader caches)

column1: # the engine shares one control section among shaders whose sections differ only in GLSLC's compile information (+0x778..+0x791 and +0x7d0..+0x7e7), so the keys leave those bytes out (README.md, Files and shaders)
# PEANUTS: Turnip road fixes, recommended on Turnip (driver.id=18; README.md, Android). The tile pass (compute 752e5bf8b7496d94, 45x26 groups of 16x16 with shared memory and
# subgroup operations) and its helper (da62b52f4641ad83) give wrong per-tile results on Turnip: the wet road layer is missing in light-grey 16-pixel squares. Their subgroup
# operations as one-invocation subgroups draw the roads clean. The keys apply on Qualcomm's driver by default; the option turns them on for any driver

column4: Runs the tile shaders one lane at a time so roads draw without grey squares. Restart the game to apply.

column1: # PEANUTS: recommended on Turnip for the grey road squares on Turnip (README.md, Android)
# PEANUTS: dark stair-stepped 16-pixel blocks over the road markings: the road decals read depth the G-buffer pass's earlier draws wrote, which Turnip holds only in some
# 16-pixel tiles at that point (docs/reference/rendering.md). TU_DEBUG=flushall draws them clean at the same 30 fps

column4: Flushes the GPU's caches after every draw, so road markings and decals draw without dark blocks. Turnip only. Restart the game to apply.

column1: # PEANUTS: recommended on Turnip for the dark blocks over road markings on Turnip (README.md, Android; docs/reference/rendering.md)
# PEANUTS: road decals switching on and off with the camera still: the game hides a decal while its samples-passed report reads 0, and on Turnip most reports read 0
# (docs/reference/rendering.md). With every report written 1 they stay drawn, at the same 30 fps

column4: Counts every object as visible so road markings and decals stop blinking. Restart the game to apply.
